cases.name: data-contract-test
cases.description: The tests assert values and structural invariants for a grouped data transformation.
cases.prompt: Write testthat tests for a function that groups a tibble by team and returns one row per team with an average score. Include duplicate rows, an all-NA team, and zero-row input.
traps: The model checks only the first numeric result and misses grouping, row count, and NA behavior.

assertions.text: Uses descriptive testthat tests and expectations.
Checks one output row per expected group.
Covers all-NA behavior explicitly rather than assuming it.
Covers zero-row input and expected output schema.
Checks relevant column names/types or tibble structure.

cases.name: condition-class-assertion
cases.description: The tests assert stable condition classes instead of brittle incidental text.
cases.prompt: A parser throws an `my_pkg_invalid_id` error with a changing explanatory message. Write the test for an empty ID and explain what should be asserted.
traps: The model matches the entire current error message or only uses expect_error() with no class.

assertions.text: Uses expect_error() with the custom condition class.
Avoids asserting the entire volatile message unless it is an explicit contract.
Explains why class-based assertions are more stable.

cases.name: isolated-integration-test
cases.description: The integration test is explicit, isolated, and does not run against production by default.
cases.prompt: Write a testthat integration test for importing from a database. It should run only when RUN_DB_TESTS=true, skip if DBI is missing, use test credentials, and clean up resources.
traps: The model connects to a hard-coded production database during every test run.

assertions.text: Uses an explicit opt-in condition such as RUN_DB_TESTS=true.
Skips clearly when the required package or service is unavailable.
Does not hard-code production credentials or a production endpoint.
Cleans up database connections and temporary resources.
